Seeing all of the diversity in the misshapen, lumpy bodies of the hamplanets that ooze over these pages from day to day, and reading about them complain how nothing ever fits them got me thinking not only about the unpredictability of the body of the insulin injector, but also the predictability of the body of a normal person. And that in turn led me to the first lines of Anna Karenina, and what Tolstoy might have said were he alive today:

Thin people are all alike. Each fat person is fat in his own way.

Tolstoy is awesome. I read him because he's pretty hardcore about animal rights, but ended up loving him for his spiritual principles. My favorite quote that relates to this sub:

There can be only one permanent revolution — a moral one; the regeneration of the inner man. How is this revolution to take place? Nobody knows how it will take place in humanity, but every man feels it clearly in himself. And yet in our world everybody thinks of changing humanity, and nobody thinks of changing himself.
